title: Make Next.js 15 fetch freshness explicit
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed lib/public-catalog.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
export async function getCatalog(){return (await fetch('https://catalog.example.com/public')).json();}
// The team assumes this fetch is persistently cached by default.

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Use an origin request counter across production requests.
Compare uncached and explicitly cached variants.
Invalidate the assigned tag from an authenticated allowed context and observe a later read.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: The absence of an explicit cache option is not evidence of persistent data caching in Next.js 15.
Use an origin request counter across production requests.
alternativeApproaches: Do not share a public catalog cache entry with personalized prices. Separate public data from tenant/user entitlements and verify all representation dimensions, authorization and HTTP cache layers.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Use an origin request counter across production requests.
Compare uncached and explicitly cached variants.
Invalidate the assigned tag from an authenticated allowed context and observe a later read.
nextjsPractice.next15: Fetch is no longer persistently cached by default. Choose force-cache, revalidation or no-store deliberately.
nextjsPractice.next16: The explicit fetch policy still matters. Cache Components adds a separate opt-in rendering/caching model; do not assume enabling it is a syntax-only migration.
